stops.note: 'a thousand paces' (double steps), about 1,480 metres; Augustus set up the Golden Milestone in the Roman Forum in 20 BC as the notional start of the empire's roads
borrowed through West Germanic (compare German Meile), probably from the milestones along Roman roads
the statute mile of 8 furlongs, 5,280 feet, was fixed by an Act of Parliament under Elizabeth I in 1593

current_meaning: a unit of distance equal to 1,760 yards (about 1.6 km)
